svg.title: Finance reports: payroll cost, spend, headcount — SoftTrack web design mockup (#135)
svg.desc: Finance → Reports draws three charts from approved runs, reimbursed expenses and compensation: payroll cost per period in each currency, spend by department against budget, and headcount against payroll growth. No conversion, no projection, and the page says where the data begins.
svg.text: Finance reports: payroll cost, spend, headcount
· hand-drawn SVG on the existing chart geometry; built by replaying real rows

g.text: , with the first approved payroll run. Nothing earlier was
recorded, so nothing earlier is drawn.
Approved run totals per month, one chart per currency. Bars are frozen line sums: later pay changes cannot redraw them.
Payroll plus reimbursed expenses. The tick is the budget.
Reports begin where the data begins, and the
page says so. A chart that quietly starts late
looks like a chart of a cheap year.
currency instance gets small multiples, never a
budget is a tick, and the Unattributed bucket is
a spreadsheet, and still without converting
anything: each currency is indexed to itself.

svg.text: Periods not yet approved are absent, not flat

g.text: The October run is still a draft, so October
is an empty slot, not a projection.

svg.text: finance admins only, like every finance page

g.text: Built from rows, not guessed backwards
sums approved run lines by period, the amounts frozen at approval (#132).
adds reimbursed expenses (#137) and compares with budgets (#134),
counts people on each approved run: active employees, replayed per period rather than
No accounting exports and no drill-down builder: the CSVs on runs and batches are the raw material for anything

svg.text: Three charts under Finance → Reports, finance-admin only, drawn as SVG on the existing chartGeometry and theme tokens (no charting library). The principles are the ticket
reports’ own: replay real rows, never run into the future, begin where the data begins and say so.
